n.story:
Your role remains one of the most physically demanding and human-centric trades, but the 'prep and plan' phase of your week is undergoing a radical shift. Instead of spending hours on a ladder with a tape measure or squinting at paper blueprints, you will use AI-powered drones and computer vision to generate perfect 3D models of a roof in minutes. These tools will automatically identify wood rot, calculate precise material orders, and even flag potential safety hazards like weak structural points before you ever step foot on the shingles.

On the job site, your expertise shifts toward high-level problem solving and precision installation. While AI can't swing a hammer or navigate a steep pitch in the wind, it will act as a 'digital foreman' in your pocket, translating complex 2D architectural plans into augmented reality (AR) overlays that show you exactly where flashing and tiles should sit. You will spend less time on logistics and waste management and more time on the skilled craftsmanship that ensures a roof is weather-tight and durable.
